warning_signs_missed: Day 9: 'Why when i ask no one answer 👀' — the client had already diagnosed our responsiveness problem in week two.
6/28: 'So the page will not go yo 0 fans' — she named the exact failure mode two days after being told to cut paid traffic; nobody put a date, owner or number against the replacement.
Five traffic chases (6/28, 7/27, 8/4, 8/10 x2), each answered with a new date and never a figure; on 8/10 she explicitly said 'worse and worse… 2 months'.
7/9: 'Otherwise, I'm not going to do the calls' — a conditional refusal of core service is a churn signal, not a process note.
Whale-trust requests (6/26, 6/30, 7/1) — the single promise that would have protected her revenue base was made and dropped.
'Is this one been solved?' (8/14) then 'Hello, is this complaint solved ?' (8/17): a client asking for the third time is checking whether to stay; both were answered with 'solved' and no screenshot.
Message volume fell from 36→10/week and hers from 14→3 in the final week; 8/17 23:58 'count from 1st- 18th' was a two-minute-warning that the period was being closed out.
Derrek's last message before the exit was 'Perfect thank you' (8/12) — the owner was absent from the account's final week.
top_fix: Never remove a client's existing traffic source without a written replacement plan that names an owner, a start date and the number we will report weekly — and then report that number every week whether it is good or bad. Vicky chased five times over 54 days and was given four dates and zero data; a single honest weekly 'new fans this week: X' (even X=0) with a call offer would have either fixed the problem or let her leave with trust intact.
